recipes.name: PBJ Cupcakes - Berry Cupcakes with Peanut Butter Frosting

steps.text: Preheat an oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Line a 12 cup muffin pan with paper baking cups. Whisk together the flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a large bowl.

Beat the butter and sugar with an electric mixer in a large bowl until fluffy, about 1 to 2 minutes. Add the egg and strawberry extract, continue beating. Beat in the milk and buttermilk, then beat in the jam. The batter should be pink.

Stir in 1/3 of the flour mixture, mixing until just incorporated. Stir in 1/2 of the remaining flour and then add the remaining flour; mixing just enough to evenly combine. Pour the batter into prepared baking cups.
Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into the cake comes clean, about 15 to 20 minutes. Cool before frosting.

Beat the peanut butter and butter until smooth in a large bowl. Mix in 2 cups of the confectioners' sugar, 1/4 cup at a time; then stir in 1/4 cup milk. Gradually add the remaining 2 cups of sugar. If the frosting is too dry add a tablespoon of milk. Frost the tops of the cooled cupcakes.

raw_recipe.headline: PBJ Cupcakes - Berry Cupcakes with Peanut Butter Frosting
raw_recipe.description: A simple pink cupcake flavored with strawberry extract and raspberry jam is frosted with creamy peanut butter frosting. Peanut butter and jelly cupcakes have all the flavor of your favorite sandwich in the sweet form of a cupcake.

video.description: The best sweets from your childhood come together in these wonderfully tempting and delicious treat! Create a berry good cupcake batter with flour, baking powder, baking soda, butter, sugar, egg, strawberry extract, milk, buttermilk and raspberry jam. When they’ve baked up all sweet fragrant, allow them to cool, then top with a generous swirl of nutty frosting made from a mixture of peanut butter, butter, confectioners’ sugar and milk. Your lunchbox favorite will never be the same.

review.reviewBody: My cakes unfortunately turned out a little drier than I like. However, the girls at the Casino loved them. I filled each one with strawberry jam to moisten them up a little.

Amazing recipe! These are the second best cupcakes I have ever tried. However, they taste like a Reese's peanut butter cup instead of PB&J. I only added 2-2.5 cups of sugar (in a batch of 24 cupcakes) for the frosting because it was losing its peanut butter flavor and creamy texture the more sugar I added. It all turned out ABSOLUTELY PERFECT in the end, and I strongly recommend the adjustment.

My co-workers requested grape jam, so that was substituted for the raspberry. Turned out so good! And I added an extra 1/4 cup of PB in the frosting and whipped it on high. Turned out to be one of the best frostings I've EVER made or had.

This peanut butter frosting is to die for if you love peanut butter! (I couldn't keep my boyfriend out of it). I split the batter into two and made half with strawberry jam and half with blackberry jam, made 10 of each with smaller cupcakes. As others have said this is a very dense cake not like a regular cupcake. I found after baking and tasting that there wasn't enough of the jam flavor for me so I cut out small holes in the middle of the cupcakes and added a little of the jams to give them more flavor, then frosted. THESE WERE A GREAT HIT (made them for my father-in-law on his birthday, he is a PB&J fanatic) Thanks for the recipe! :) I will make these again!
Good, but I will quarter the sugar and double the peanut butter in the frosting next time. I made the frosting with 2c powdered sugar and 1/2c peanut butter and cannot taste the peanut butter!

I didn't have strawberry extract, so I substituted Raspberry coffee syrup 2tsp since it's less concentrated flavor. The cupcakes are moist and flavorful. For the frosting, I used 3 cups powdered sugar because that's all I had. I only used 2TBSP milk and added 2 TBSP peanut butter coffee syrup. The cupcakes with the frosting are just perfect.
Super moist! I used about half the icing sugar for the frosting and had more than enough icing for the batch.I also substituted strawberry extract for vanilla. Delish!

Well, I only made the frosting, to use on my favorite chocolate cake, and it was great, got compliments all around. I found I only needed 2 1/2 cups of powdered sugar, plenty sweet enough. Also, it made the perfect amount for a 2 layer cake.

Great recipe. I used the ingredients for 36 cupcakes, followed the directions to a T with the exception of the Strawberry Extract and instead used LORANN OILS Strawberry Flavor. Cupcakes and frosting are not overly sweet, they were just right and together tasted like a Peanut Butter and Jelly sandwich. Will make again!!

These cupcakes really taste as good as I had hoped. Made a few tweaks though. I used vanilla extract instead of strawberry, and 4 cups of powdered sugar for frosting is just ridiculous. I used half and the frosting was more than sweet enough. Next time I might even use less. Really does taste like a sweet pb&j

I made a double batch of these and took them to work, and they loved them! You must like peanut butter to enjoy these, the frosting definitely has a strong peanut butter taste. I couldn't find any strawberry extract at my grocery store, so I used raspberry instead. I stuck with the raspberry jam.
It was very good but I would recommend to use less sugar
I noticed that they turned out more like muffins than cupcakes but they were still delicious

I made this for my children's birthday party, and everyone really loved them. I thought the PB frosting was amazing, and think it would taste really good on a chocolate cupcake. The berry cupcake was okay. Even with strawberry extract and raspberry jam, it didn't have a lot of flavor. And it was not a pink color; the batter was whitish, then the raspberry jam turned it a slightly red color. However, after baking it was a slightly purple/gray color. If it were a pink color and had more berry flavor it would have been better, but was all right.
Yum! I used vanilla extract instead of strawberry because I couldn't find it anywhere.
It looks delicious and I would recommend people to make it only if they want to but I don't have all the ingredients.

I switched it around, used raspberry extract and strawberry jam. I found them way too sweet with the frosting, and kind of bitter (too much baking powder?) without. Kids ate them up, luckily, but I don't think I'll be making again - the next day had turned very gluey in consistency.

I only made the frosting. I overall thought this frosting was decent. It tastes delicious but it is a little too sugary. Also it is way too thick! It was very hard to frost with. The cupcakes did end up looking nice though.
The frosting was delicious but a bit overpowering.

Excellent recipe - came in second place in a cupcake contest with this recipe. The cupcakes are nice and moist, the frosting is AMAZING. Filled the cupcakes with strawberry jam and sprinkled crushed up potato chips on the top (it sounds gross, but I promise it's delicious!!). Thanks for the recipe!!
